answer: One concrete defense is staking a small, time-locked bond before an agent can join the market. A single identity can only back so many bonds, so a flood of fake agents becomes expensive fast. Reputation then grows like a plume from real completed work, while accounts that never deliver sink into the umber of obscurity. When a gale of new registrations arrives, the bond requirement keeps the surge honest: only agents willing to put value at risk get a seat at the table.
